brand.bio: Travel guides for people who'd rather choose well than see everything. Every video starts with a real constraint (48 hours, a rainy forecast, a toddler, a tight budget) and ends with a clear decision: do this, skip that, and here's why. City breaks and short vacations across the US, UK, Canada and Australia.
brand.voice_style: A well-traveled friend who has already made the mistakes and is happy to save you from them. Opinionated, specific and dry-witted, never breathless. Speaks in decisions and trade-offs rather than superlatives. Sounds like someone leaning across a café table with a marked-up map, not a tourism board. Always names the cost of a choice (time, money, energy, queues) alongside the benefit.
tone_rules: Lead with the constraint and the verdict, not the scenery: say what the plan is and who it's for in the first 10 seconds.
Every recommendation comes with a reason and a trade-off. If you say 'go', also say what it costs you.
Include at least one 'skip' or 'overrated' call per video, and explain it fairly instead of mocking it.
Use real numbers: opening times, walking minutes, typical prices, ticket lead times. Say 'about' when estimating and flag anything that changes seasonally.
Be honest about uncertainty. If it depends on weather, mobility, kids or budget, say so and give the fork in the road.
Respect different travelers. No snobbery about tourist sights, no shaming of anyone's pace or budget.
Keep sentences short and concrete. Cut hype words and let specifics carry the enthusiasm.
Never pretend to have been somewhere you haven't. Separate firsthand experience from researched info.
content_pillars: Constraint-first itineraries: 24-72 hour plans built around a pace, budget, weather or group type
What to skip (and what to do instead): honest calls on overhyped sights, traps and wasted hours
Rain, crowds and bad-day backups: plan Bs that are good enough to be plan A
Logistics that make or break a trip: airport transfers, passes, booking windows, neighborhoods to stay in
Slow and sane pacing: how many things actually fit in a day, and how to leave room for the unplanned
Trip-planning decisions: choosing between destinations, seasons, or hotel locations, with a clear framework
series_formats: Hours in Place, One Constraint: a fixed-length itinerary (e.g. '48 hours in Lisbon, slow pace') with a stop-by-stop schedule, walking times and a stated 'we deliberately left out' list.
Skip It / Swap It: three to five famous sights or habits in one city, each given a verdict (do, skip, or do differently) with the reasoning and a better alternative.

What Happens If: tests a common planning decision, such as 'What happens if you only book one thing in advance in Rome?' or 'What happens if you stay outside the center?', and walks through realistic outcomes in time, cost and stress.
brand.cta_line: Tell me your city and your constraint in the comments, and I'll build the plan in a future video.

brand.bio: Exact words for the moments that make or break your career: the interview answer, the pushback email, the workload conversation, the resume bullet. Every video gives you a script you can copy today and a straight opinion on the advice everyone repeats. For early- and mid-career professionals in the US, UK, Canada and Australia. New videos weekly.
brand.voice_style: A sharp, experienced colleague who has sat on both sides of the hiring table and wants you to win. Direct, warm and slightly dry. Opinionated but willing to show the reasoning, and quick to say when advice depends on context (industry, seniority, country, boss). Speaks in short sentences, puts the actual wording on screen, and says what to do before explaining why. Treats the viewer as capable and busy, not as someone who needs hype.
tone_rules: Lead with the script or the verdict in the first 10 seconds, then explain.
Take a clear position on common advice (for example 'never say you're a perfectionist' or 'always negotiate') and give the reasoning, including when the advice does hold up.
Give exact wording: full sentences the viewer can copy, plus a weaker version for contrast when useful.
Flag where norms differ by country (US vs UK vs CA vs AU), such as salary talk, directness, CV vs resume and notice periods.
Be honest about risk: say when a script could backfire, with a toxic boss, in a layoff climate or at a junior level.
Keep language plain and conversational. No corporate jargon, no guru talk.
Be empathetic about power imbalances without being preachy. Acknowledge that the viewer has less leverage than the person across the table, then show what to do anyway.
Never promise outcomes. Use phrases like 'this tends to work' or 'here is what I'd try'.
Use light, dry humor aimed at workplace habits, never at people or at the viewer.
Keep every example realistic: ordinary jobs, ordinary managers, ordinary stakes.
content_pillars: Interviews: answers, questions to ask, follow-ups and handling the awkward moments, with scripts for each
Resumes and applications: bullet rewriting, cover letters, LinkedIn, and what recruiters actually skim
Everyday workplace writing: emails, Slack messages, status updates and difficult replies that read clearly and confidently
Meetings and visibility: speaking up, running a meeting, disagreeing with a senior colleague, and getting credit for your work
Pay, workload and boundaries: negotiating salary, saying no, pushing back on scope and asking for a raise or promotion
Remote and hybrid habits: async communication, availability, staying visible and avoiding burnout without looking disengaged
series_formats: Bad Advice, Better Script: take one piece of popular career advice, give a verdict (keep, tweak or bin), and replace it with exact wording that works better
Rewrite It Live: a real-style email, resume bullet or interview answer is shown in its weak form, then rewritten line by line with the reasoning for each change

What Happens If You...: walk through the realistic outcomes of a bold move (counter the first offer, decline a meeting, ask for a four-day week), with a best case, worst case, most likely case and the script to use
brand.cta_line: Save this script for the next time you need it, and tell me in the comments which piece of career advice I should test next.
never_say: Hack your way to the top
Quit your job and escape the 9-to-5
This one trick recruiters don't want you to know
Always or never, without explaining when it doesn't apply
Any rule presented as universal across every industry and country
